sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental legal tradition with strong French influence; commercial and company law codified)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaties concluded with more than 90 sovereign states (including the United States, China, Hong Kong SAR, the United Arab Emirates, Canada, and Singapore)
Double Taxation Agreements with more than 85 jurisdictions (including the United States, Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland)
EU internal market freedoms and EU international trade agreements directly applicable in Luxembourg by virtue of European Union law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on beneficial ownership identification; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce, company register and accounting; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing professional obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent extract from the foreign commercial register of a corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or commercial register in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners and proposed directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority and local municipal or utility records of the respective country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder or director entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry or state authority in the shareholder's or director entity's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of lawful source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or foreign equivalent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified sworn translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish of all non-native source documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator accredited before the Luxembourg courts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and designated signatories against the CSSF AML/CFT framework, the Law of 12 November 2004, CSSF Regulation 12-02, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Nations Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the domestic Luxembourg national sanctions list, and the FATF statement list; Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and non-EEA resident UBOs trigger enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, prior to signing of the notarial deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible electronically at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory documents and filings may be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish; the RCS accepts company names in Latin script and requires a transliteration into Latin characters for any foreign-script name; the mandatory legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the company name; the name must be distinctive and not misleading under Article 5-1 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce, company register and accounting.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg and its derivatives (Luxembourg, Lëtzebuerg, Lux, LU) requiring prior ministerial or government authorization
Bank / Banque / Banking institutions requiring CSSF prior authorization
Insurance / Assurance / Réassurance requiring CAA (Commissariat aux Assurances) prior authorization
Investment fund / Fonds d'investissement / FIS / SICAV requiring CSSF authorization
Stock exchange / Bourse / regulated market terminology
Trust / Fiducie / foundation terms reserved for regulated legal forms
Lawyer / Avocat / Notary / Auditor terminology reserved to regulated professions
Any name contrary to public order, good morals, or creating confusion with an existing RCS-registered entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a written rejection notice issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recours) before the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement), composed as the court with jurisdiction over the commercial register; the appeal must attach the RCS refusal notification, the proposed company name, the completed name-reservation form, and a draft of the articles of association; alternatively, where the refusal arises from a near-identical existing registration, the applicant may submit a new name reservation with a materially differentiating element on the LBR electronic portal, and may, if the conflicting registration is fraudulent or infringing, petition for deletion of the conflicting mark under the Law of 19 December 2002 and applicable unfair competition rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted; a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) may serve as the statutory registered office, but the SARL must maintain genuine and verifiable operational commercial substance in Luxembourg, such as a physical operational location, employees, a third-party fulfillment center, or local management; a bare virtual mail-forwarding address without any real operational presence is not accepted by the RCS or the CSSF for an active e-commerce retail business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; annualized probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is estimated at 5–10% for a standard-risk online retail SARL, increasing to 15–25% where the ultimate beneficial owner is resident outside the EEA or where the registered office is shared within a multi-client domiciliation provider and such providers are subject to enhanced CSSF monitoring.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and name reservation fee via the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic filing tariff published by the LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and related notary verifications
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff composed of a statutory minimum fee plus proportional scale on share capital; prevailing market range EUR 900–2,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and coordinated electronic publication in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and publication tariff applicable to new company filings

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of ultimate beneficial owners with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Exempt from filing fees under current RBE regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 1,500–2,500 per annum including handling of statutory correspondence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization fees for the foreign corporate and shareholder document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document's country of origin under the Hague Apostille Convention
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of approximately EUR 20–60 per document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of source documents into French, German, or Luxembourgish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of EUR 60–120 per translated page with a minimum per-document fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External AML/KYC counsel fee for UBO identification, PEP and sanctions screening, and compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a fixed-scope pre-incorporation AML/CFT compliance package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales), Title V, Articles 710-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), acting with the enrolled Luxembourg notary and municipal authorities
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised instrument of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed. At least 25% (EUR 3,000) must be paid up at incorporation by deposit into a blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution or a notary escrow account; the depository issues a bank certificate for the notary. The balance is callable by the managers within five years. No sector-specific capital escrow applies to ISIC 4791 online retail.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription of 12,000 shares of EUR 1.00 each by the founding shareholder for an aggregate par value of EUR 12,000. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [Luxembourg address], and that the managers be authorised to register this address with the RCS. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] be appointed as managers (gérants) of the Company, each with full authority to manage and represent the Company in accordance with the articles of association. RESOLVED, that the managers be delegated to complete all filings, filings with the RCS, and statutory formalities necessary for incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and availability verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS name availability window via MyRCS / guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic request for a negative certificate to verify the availability of the proposed corporate name. The application must include one principal name and three fallback options. Once issued, the certificate reserves the name for a short period. The certificate must be delivered to the notary before execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the proposed shareholder(s)
Power of attorney of the founder, if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the certificate because the name is already reserved or too similar, file a reasoned administrative re-application and submit alternative names; the certificate can be reissued on the corrected name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of notarised articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg (enrolled notary of the founders' choice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the SARL statutes in French or German, including corporate object, capital, registered office, management powers and duration. Arrange an appointment before a Luxembourg notary, where the founding shareholder(s) or their attorney execute the deed. The notary verifies legal capacity, capital, and the absence of a negative certificate blocking registration. The notary documents the deed and enters the preliminary registration data in the RCS workflow.
required_dossiers: Passports or ID cards of shareholders and officers
Proof of physical address of shareholders
Bank certificate or escrow statement of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS pre-query identifies a defect in the proposed articles, the notary issues a rectification proposal; the shareholders execute an amending resolution or a fresh deed with the corrected wording before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum paid-up capital in a Luxembourg blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary's escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit at least EUR 3,000 (or a higher amount if provided by the articles). The bank issues a deposit certificate specifying that the funds are blocked for the incorporation. The certificate is forwarded to the notary and to the RCS. After RCS registration, the funds are released to the company.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owner declaration and AML screening forms
Power of attorney for bank account opening
Preliminary articles of association or notarised draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or rejects the deposit due to incomplete KYC, supplement the requested information and resubmit; a new bank certificate will be issued once the deposit is confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the RCS and registration of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or authorised counsel submits the notarised deed and coordinated articles through the RCS online portal, together with the registration form, manager consents, and bank certificate. The RCS validates the dossier, assigns the Luxembourg registration number (RCS number), and the company acquires legal personality upon entry in the register. The state filing fee is paid online.
required_dossiers: Consent of managers to their appointment
Criminal record certificate or equivalent declaration for each manager
Proof of business address / registered office lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond with corrected documentation within the prescribed deadline; if registration is refused, remedy the specific defect and file a new application; administrative refusal may be appealed before the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RES publication department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration is completed, the notary or counsel instructs the RCS to publish the statutory particulars in the RES. The publication includes the company name, legal form, registered office, corporate object, subscribed capital, managerial powers, and RCS number. The publication is available online and constitutes the formal notice to third parties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES publication contains an inaccuracy, request a corrected publication by filing a supplemental certificate from the notary; the RCS will replace the erroneous text and re-publish within a short period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and beneficial ownership formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number if taxable sales will exceed the statutory thresholds; register as a social security employer with the CCSS if hiring staff; obtain an EORI number for any import of auto parts; and file the ultimate beneficial owner information with the RBO.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming release of capital
Beneficial owner details and declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social registrations are delayed, contact the dedicated case handler and submit corrected forms; any assessed penalty for late registration can be cured by written explanation and payment of the minimal administrative fine before the AEDT director.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de l'industrie (not applicable to pure online retail under ISIC 4791)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate manufacturing or operating licence required for online retail of automotive aftermarket parts and tuning accessories; a municipal building/occupancy permit may be needed for any warehouse or office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category exempt / no EIA required for pure online retail activities. If the company stores batteries, waste oils, or other dangerous substances on site, a classed establishment notification or authorisation under the Law of 10 July 2017 on the integrated environmental approach may be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges for e-commerce operations. Warehouse logistics must comply with municipal waste separation obligations, EU Directive 2008/98/EC waste handling requirements, and if hazardous substances are stored, technical rules for storage of dangerous goods (TRGS 510). VOC emissions, if any, are limited under Directive 2010/75/EU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for occupied premises under the Luxembourg fire protection code, structural load inspection for storage racks, and workplace occupational health clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including a written risk assessment and employee health surveillance where staff are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; registration portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu) and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). VAT is administered by Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via the eCDF (electronic filing) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first complete notarial incorporation and register with the RCS/LBR; the Luxembourg Business Registers assigns a business registration number. Thereafter, the SARL must apply to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for a Luxembourg national tax number (numéro d'identification national / matricule) and to the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA for a VAT identification number (numéro de TVA LU). The VAT application is filed on MyGuichet.lu / eCDF, supported by the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, proof of registered office address, RCS extract, identity of directors/managers, and a description of intended activities. Non-resident shareholders may appoint a local tax representative for procedural service; the VAT number is generally issued within 1–2 weeks. Registration thresholds are mandatory from the first taxable transaction; no economic substance minimum is imposed solely for TIN issuance, but ongoing substance requirements apply under domestic and EU law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg SARLs are opaque corporate taxpayers subject to CIT at entity level; no check-the-box pass-through election exists under domestic law. Luxembourg has transposed ATAD hybrid mismatch rules (law of 27 December 2018) denying deductions for hybrid mismatches and requiring entity characterisation consistent with Luxembourg tax classification. A SARL may elect to join a Luxembourg fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) regime only if it meets the 95% participation threshold and other statutory conditions; an EU/EEA parent with a Luxembourg branch may also elect the EU/EEA fiscal unity regime, filing a joint election with the tax administration. A SARL whose activities qualify may elect the special IP box regime (80% exemption) and the investment credit regime. For VAT, no elective registration is available where turnover exceeds the mandatory threshold; small businesses below EUR 35,000 may elect the VAT franchise regime (exemption without input VAT recovery), but an export-oriented auto parts retailer would normally elect normal VAT taxable status to recover input VAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for goods and services (domestic small-business franchise exemption); mandatory VAT registration from the first euro of taxable supplies for EU-distance sales of goods or import transactions, subject to the EUR 10,000 Union threshold for cross-border remote sales where the supplier may opt for the destination-state registration. A foreign e-commerce seller with no Luxembourg establishment must register if it performs distance sales to Luxembourg consumers exceeding EUR 35,000 or if it holds stock in Luxembourg and makes local supplies exceeding EUR 35,000; otherwise it may register via the non-union or union OSS procedure for pan-EU distance sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate a continuous transaction control (CTC) real-time clearance model. E-invoicing is permitted and legally accepted, but no government fiscal stamping, real-time API filing, or mandatory clearance of each invoice is required. All taxable persons must retain auditable records for six years, and B2B invoices must satisfy EU VAT invoicing rules (mandatory content under Article 226 of Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed). Businesses must file monthly/quarterly VAT returns electronically via eCDF, submit recapitulative statements (Intrastat/ECS) for EU dispatches, and may use the OSS portal for distance sales. Practical e-commerce platforms may require electronic exchange of structured invoices (Peppol/UBL), but this is contractual, not a statutory fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 146 of Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed in Luxembourg VAT law. A Luxembourg-based auto-parts retailer may zero-rate physical goods dispatched or transported to a third country (outside the EU) provided that: (i) the goods leave the EU within the statutory timeframe and are substantiated by transport documents; (ii) the supplier receives the goods at its Luxembourg premises or the supply is linked to dispatched goods; (iii) the customer is established abroad and title/risk has passed; and (iv) the supplier holds commercial, transport, and customs evidence proving actual movement out of the EU. Services linked to exported goods (transport, ancillary handling) may also be zero-rated/outside scope under place-of-supply rules. Supplies of goods to EU destinations are not zero-rated but are exempt/remarked as intra-Community supplies subject to the customer's VAT ID and the recapitulative statement, provided the customer is VAT-registered. Retail online sales of auto parts to non-VAT-registered EU consumers are distance sales taxed at destination via OSS at the applicable member-state rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg export customs declaration (export summary declaration and Export Declaration via Luxembourg's customs IT system, linked to the UCC Single Administrative Document status, exit confirmation from the customs office of exit in the EU member state of exit, or the AES export declaration)

Bill of Lading (maritime) or Air Waybill (air freight), or CMR consignment note (road haulage) with signature/delivery receipt, and where applicable the carrier's warehouse receipt or parcel tracking proof of physical delivery outside the EU

Proof of payment and inward remittance/foreign exchange repatriation certificate showing settlement of the export sale in foreign currency, or equivalent bank transfer confirmation evidencing payment received from the foreign buyer (where goods are sold to third-country customers)
Commercial invoice, proforma invoice, and packing list describing the goods, HS/CN codes, quantities, and export sale terms (Incoterms)
Certificate of origin (EUR.1/ATR or statement on origin) where preferential origin is claimed under EU trade agreements
Proof of identity/VAT status of the foreign customer (e.g., company registry extract or import certificate where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax and customs administrations may retrospectively deny zero-rating if the documentary evidence does not prove, within the deadline and to the required standard, that goods physically left the EU and that title passed to the third-country buyer. Consequences include: assessment of Luxembourg VAT at the standard rate (17%) with default interest at 0.6% per month or pro-rata period rate as prescribed, fines of up to EUR 250,000 for serious VAT evasion/infringement under the general tax law (Abgabenordnung) and specific VAT law, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent export claims, falsification of documents, or declaration of false statements. Under the EU Customs Code and national customs rules, false customs declarations may result in customs penalties and reputational consequences; the VAT clawback period is generally five years (ten years in cases of tax fraud or in the absence of good-faith filing). Export zero-rating claims must be supported by contemporaneous evidence retained for at least six years; missing proof triggers immediate VAT liability and penalty assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the national central bank of the Eurosystem and agent of the European Central Bank in Luxembourg; prudential licensing and supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and e-money institutions rest with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Ministry of Finance retains statutory competence for financial-sector legislation and sanctions implementation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg implements Article 63 TFEU free movement of capital and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation; no prior exchange-control authorization applies to equity injections, dividend distributions, loan repayments, trade payments or profit repatriation. Dividend remittance hurdles are tax-legal, not FX-legal: a SARL distribution must satisfy the balance-sheet and solvency test (net assets cannot fall below subscribed capital plus non-distributable reserves under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies) and must be approved by the shareholders' meeting; the domestic 15% dividend withholding tax is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10%, or by applicable double-tax treaties with rates dependent on ownership levels. No material practical hurdles exist for converting EUR into USD, GBP or offshore RMB (CNH), and banks execute lawful client conversions on demand.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation deadline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no surrender obligation for export receipts. The SARL may retain all e-commerce proceeds in EUR, USD or CNH multicurrency accounts indefinitely. Binding obligations are limited to: accurate bookkeeping and valuation of foreign-currency receivables under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS; BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations on cross-border flows above reporting thresholds; EU recapitulative VAT statements for intra-Community supplies and EORI/customs documentation for extra-EU imports; and standard AML record-retention of trade-documentation bundles.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) / Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) / Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) / Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a collection and disbursement overlay, Low as the primary treasury rail. EEA-authorized electronic money institutions (e.g., Airwallex, Wise, Revolut Business, Qonto) may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and provide multi-currency IBANs, faster payments and cross-border disbursement; they are legally prohibited from issuing the notarial capital-deposit certificate required for SARL formation, do not provide commercial documentary credits, outright FX forwards or NDFs or ISDA derivative execution, and client balances are not covered by the Luxembourg statutory deposit-guarantee scheme. Post-Brexit UK EMIs cannot passport under PSD2 and may only transact on a reverse-solicitation basis, making them ill-suited for an operating treasury. Daily sweeps from any EMI balance to the tier-1 Luxembourg bank are mandatory to control counterparty and de-risking exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one director and each UBO must complete a compliance interview; for a Low_Risk_Standard profile with EU/EEA or treaty-classified non-resident shareholders, tier-1 banks accept a full remote procedure composed of: notarized and apostilled corporate documents (incorporation deed or draft, articles of association, board resolution on account opening); RBE extract and CSSF-compliant identity verification via certified passport copies; live video-call interview with the relationship manager; and source-of-funds bank letters. BGL BNP Paribas, BIL and BCEE may nevertheless require one physical appearance in Luxembourg where UBOs reside in non-EU jurisdictions not covered by FATF-compliant regimes. The notary receives the capital-deposit certificate directly from the bank electronically, so physical attendance at a branch is not strictly mandatory for the formation escrow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border card-not-present e-commerce transaction velocity disproportionate to the SARL's €12,000 minimum statutory capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Incorporation deed and RBE extract; 13 months of Stripe and PayPal settlement statements; signed PSP merchant agreements; detailed product catalogue mapped to ISIC 4791 and NAICS 441310; 3-year cash-flow and profit-forecast model; refund and chargeback policy; supplier contract list; confirmation of treasury concentration at a Luxembourg credit institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident shareholding chain or UBO identification gaps involving nominee, trust or multi-tier holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RBE extract; full corporate-structure chart; certificates of incorporation and good standing for each intermediate entity; incumbency certificates; passports notarized and apostilled; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; sworn UBO attestation excluding nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparency and substance concerns triggering CRS and FATCA classification friction for the Luxembourg entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax-residence certificate issued by the Administration des contributions directes; filed annual accounts at the RCSL; VAT registration certificate; registered-office lease; substance evidence including management presence, board minutes and decision log; CRS and FATCA self-certification forms; transfer-pricing policy under OECD standards for cross-border parts purchases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement flows arriving from third-party payment aggregators (Stripe, PayPal) rather than direct customer bank transfers, creating AML-source ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-flow schematic; processor settlement schedules; daily merchant statements; merchant identification and processing-account documentation; internal AML/CFT controls manual; sanctions and PEP screening logs; written undertaking to consolidate daily receivables into the main Luxembourg operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use export-control exposure for automotive electronics and performance parts under EU Regulation 2021/821.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product technical datasheets; completed dual-use classification matrix; denied-party screening evidence; end-user and anti-diversion undertakings from major wholesale customers; distribution-policy confirmation excluding sanctioned and embargoed territories; compliance-officer attestation accompanying each supplier contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, the SARL's €12,000 minimum capital must be fully subscribed and paid in cash prior to the notarial deed. Routing protocol: open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) with BGL BNP Paribas, BIL or BCEE in the name of the SARL in formation; execute an inbound SWIFT MT103 from the shareholders' or UBOs' verified bank accounts, quoting the draft-deed reference and the BCL purpose code 'F1 - Participation au capital / prise de participation'; the receiving bank issues the capital-deposit certificate (attestation de consignation) directly to the Luxembourg notary; after incorporation, the blocked account converts into the operating account and the RBE registration is filed; subsequent equity injections or share-premium (agio) payments from foreign parents are routed by MT103 with purpose code F1 or F13, accompanied by a board resolution, RBE extract and source-of-funds letters to pre-empt AML review. All transactions are reported by the bank to BCL balance-of-payments statistics; cash settlements exceeding €10,000 between professionals are prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories are cleared via: SWIFT MT103 international transfers for non-EU suppliers (China, Taiwan, United States), citing BCL goods-purpose codes and the supplier invoice and EORI numbers; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) issued by BGL BNP Paribas, BIL or BCEE for large containerized purchases, with MT700 issuance and MT202/MT103 cover payments; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (up to €100,000 per transaction) for EU/EEA suppliers; offshore RMB (CNH) settlement through the Bank of China (Luxembourg) S.A. clearing branch, with cross-border CNY payments executed via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) for mainland China factory settlements; multicurrency EUR/USD/CNH accounts with notional zero-balancing pooling and an intraday liquidity sweep to the main operational account; and Stripe/PayPal mass-payout APIs for customer refunds, chargebacks and marketplace net settlements. The bank's electronic platform provides same-day local EUR execution and an audit trail of purpose codes for every cross-border disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/GBP) executed with a MiFID II-authorized Luxembourg or EU credit institution under an ISDA 1992 or 2002 Master Agreement or local short-form confirmation
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore CNY (EUR/CNY) where physical delivery is unavailable, subject to ISDA 2002 Schedule, CSA margin terms and EMIR transaction reporting
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY / CCIRS) for matched asset-liability currency hedging between EUR settlement positions and USD or CNH procurement payables
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (puts and calls) for procurement-budget protection, with immediate trade reconciliation and EMIR disclosure to a licensed trade repository
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity conversion between EUR, USD and CNH, permitted with any CSSF-authorized credit institution under the bank's treasury lines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (balance sheet, profit and loss, notes and, when required, management report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the annual general meeting; the AGM must be held within six months of the financial year-end (for a calendar-year SARL, the latest practical filing date is 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; criminal liability for managing directors; order by the Public Prosecutor to file; persistent non-filing may trigger judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (RBE) Confirmation – annual conformity check of beneficial ownership data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual general meeting approving the annual accounts; the AGM must be held within six months of the financial year-end (for a calendar-year SARL, the latest practical filing date is 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and criminal sanctions; knowingly incorrect data may be treated as a false declaration, and serious or repeated breaches can lead to judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 September of the calendar year following the tax year; extensions may be granted until 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; administrative fines up to EUR 1,000; ex officio assessment by the ACD with penalties up to 20% of the tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if, on the balance sheet date, the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 4,400,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,800,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. A statutory audit is also required for public-interest entities, financial-sector professionals, and where the articles of association or shareholders impose a higher level of control.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 18 December 2015 on the annual accounts of undertakings, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts. Consolidated accounts of public-interest entities follow IFRS-EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Luxembourg SARL must confirm the RBE-registered beneficial ownership information annually within one month after the shareholders' meeting approving the annual accounts. Any shareholding transfer or other UBO change must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the event; the annual confirmation serves as a mandatory data review and refresh.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (progressive CIT under Article 115 LIR: 15% on taxable income up to EUR 175,000; 16% on income between EUR 175,001 and EUR 200,000; 17% above EUR 200,000), plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) at the Luxembourg City rate of 6.75%, producing a combined top statutory headline rate of approximately 24.94% (before the deductibility of the municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (Article 166 LIR): 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% (or, for certain capital gains, an acquisition cost of at least EUR 6,000,000) held for at least 12 months. IP box regime (Article 50ter LIR): 80% exemption of qualifying IP-derived income, reducing the effective CIT rate to approximately 5.2% on such income, subject to nexus substance requirements. Notional interest deduction (NID): deduction of a notional interest on qualifying new equity contributions, at a rate published annually by the ACD. Investment tax credits (crédit d'impôt investissement) for qualifying tangible fixed assets in Luxembourg. Loss carryforward is unlimited in time but capped annually at EUR 1,000,000 plus 17.5% of the taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; no carryback is permitted.
